question.text: A crossing guard's directions differ from the traffic light. Whom do you obey?

answer.text: When a police officer, school crossing guard or other worker directs traffic with a sign, you must obey that person even if a traffic light or road sign says something different.

teaching.text: A person directing traffic outranks any light or sign. Remember: Obey the person directing.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: When a police officer, school crossing guard or other worker directs traffic with a sign, you must obey that person even if a traffic light or road sign says something different.

question.text: What colors and shape do most warning signs have, and what do they tell you?

answer.text: Warning signs are yellow with black words or symbols, most are diamond shaped, and they alert you to a hazard or special situation ahead.

teaching.text: Yellow with black symbols, usually a diamond, means a hazard or special situation ahead. Remember: Yellow diamond warns ahead.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Warning signs are yellow with black words or symbols, most are diamond shaped, and they alert you to a hazard or special situation ahead.

question.text: What does an Intersection or Cross Road warning sign mark?

answer.text: An Intersection or Cross Road warning sign marks a spot ahead where two or more roads cross each other.

teaching.text: Crossing roads ahead mean more traffic to watch for. Remember: Roads cross ahead.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: An Intersection or Cross Road warning sign marks a spot ahead where two or more roads cross each other.

question.text: What does a Divided Highway sign mean?

answer.text: A Divided Highway sign means opposing lanes ahead will be separated by a physical barrier such as a guardrail.

teaching.text: A barrier such as a guardrail will separate the opposing lanes ahead. Remember: Barrier will split traffic.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A Divided Highway sign means opposing lanes ahead will be separated by a physical barrier such as a guardrail.

question.text: What does a Slippery When Wet sign tell you to do?

answer.text: A Slippery When Wet sign means the pavement ahead may be slick, so reduce your speed.

teaching.text: Slick pavement may be ahead, so ease off. Remember: Slick ahead, slow down.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A Slippery When Wet sign means the pavement ahead may be slick, so reduce your speed.

question.text: What does a Signal Ahead sign warn about?

answer.text: A Signal Ahead sign warns of traffic lights ahead, so be prepared to slow and stop.

teaching.text: Traffic lights are coming, so be ready to slow and stop. Remember: Lights ahead, be ready.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A Signal Ahead sign warns of traffic lights ahead, so be prepared to slow and stop.

question.text: What does a Deer Crossing sign mark?

answer.text: A Deer Crossing sign marks an area where deer very often cross the road, so stay alert.

teaching.text: Deer cross often in the area, so keep scanning. Remember: Deer often cross, stay alert.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A Deer Crossing sign marks an area where deer very often cross the road, so stay alert.

question.text: What does a Lane Ends sign show, and what should you do?

answer.text: A Lane Ends sign shows which lane is ending; move into the remaining lane once it is safe.

teaching.text: Your lane is ending; move over when it is safe. Remember: Your lane ends, move over.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A Lane Ends sign shows which lane is ending; move into the remaining lane once it is safe.

question.text: What does a Curved Road sign warn about?

answer.text: A Curved Road sign warns that the road bends gradually right or left, and you slow only as much as needed to drive it safely.

teaching.text: A gradual bend means slowing only as much as needed. Remember: Gradual bend, ease off.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A Curved Road sign warns that the road bends gradually right or left, and you slow only as much as needed to drive it safely.

question.text: How does a Sharp Turn sign differ from a Curved Road sign?

answer.text: A Sharp Turn sign can point left or right and asks you to be ready to slow for the turn, unlike a Curved Road sign, which marks a gradual bend.

teaching.text: A sharp turn calls for more slowing than a gentle curve. Remember: Sharp turn, slow more.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A Sharp Turn sign can point left or right and asks you to be ready to slow for the turn, unlike a Curved Road sign, which marks a gradual bend.

question.text: How does a Merge sign differ from a Lane Ends sign?

answer.text: A Merge sign shows a lane joining from the right or left, while a Lane Ends sign shows your own lane ending; in both cases you move over when it is safe.

teaching.text: Merge means another lane joins; Lane Ends means yours stops. Remember: Merge joins, lane ends yours.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A Merge sign shows a lane joining from the right or left, while a Lane Ends sign shows your own lane ending; in both cases you move over when it is safe.

question.text: What does a Hill sign warn of?

answer.text: A Hill sign warns of a hill ahead, and you slow down if needed to stay safe.

teaching.text: A hill is ahead, so slow down if needed. Remember: Hill ahead, slow if needed.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A Hill sign warns of a hill ahead, and you slow down if needed to stay safe.

question.text: Where does a Two-Way Traffic sign appear?

answer.text: A two-Way Traffic sign appears where a one-way road ends and you enter a road carrying traffic in both directions.

teaching.text: Leaving a one-way road, expect traffic from the other direction. Remember: One-way ends, traffic both ways.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A two-Way Traffic sign appears where a one-way road ends and you enter a road carrying traffic in both directions.

question.text: What does a Stop Ahead sign show, and what does it ask you to do?

answer.text: A Stop Ahead sign shows an arrow with a stop-sign shape beneath it and tells you to slow so you can stop safely at the stop sign ahead.

teaching.text: A stop sign is ahead, so start slowing now. Remember: Stop sign ahead, slow.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A Stop Ahead sign shows an arrow with a stop-sign shape beneath it and tells you to slow so you can stop safely at the stop sign ahead.

question.text: How does a Roundabout Ahead sign look?

answer.text: A Roundabout Ahead sign is a diamond with a counterclockwise symbol above a rectangular plaque reading Roundabout Ahead.

teaching.text: The counterclockwise symbol and plaque mean a roundabout is coming. Remember: Counterclockwise symbol, plaque below.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A Roundabout Ahead sign is a diamond with a counterclockwise symbol above a rectangular plaque reading Roundabout Ahead.

question.text: What does the arrow plaque on a Pedestrian Crossing sign show, and what must you do?

answer.text: A Pedestrian Crossing sign has an arrow plaque below the walker symbol showing where the crossing is, and you must yield to anyone crossing.

teaching.text: The arrow shows the crossing, and you yield to anyone using it. Remember: Arrow shows crossing; yield.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A Pedestrian Crossing sign has an arrow plaque below the walker symbol showing where the crossing is, and you must yield to anyone crossing.

question.text: What colors may school zone and school crossing signs be, and what must you do there?

answer.text: School zone and school crossing signs may be fluorescent green or yellow, and you must yield to pedestrians crossing there.

teaching.text: Bright green or yellow school signs mean yield to crossing pedestrians. Remember: Fluorescent green or yellow; yield.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: School zone and school crossing signs may be fluorescent green or yellow, and you must yield to pedestrians crossing there.

question.text: What do regulatory signs do, and what shapes and colors do they use?

answer.text: Regulatory signs state the rules of the road; they are square, rectangular or a special shape and white or red with black, red, white or green lettering.

teaching.text: White or red signs state rules you must obey. Remember: Rules in white or red.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Regulatory signs state the rules of the road; they are square, rectangular or a special shape and white or red with black, red, white or green lettering.

question.text: What does a Do Not Enter sign mean, and where is it posted?

answer.text: A Do Not Enter sign means you may not go in; it is posted on one-way streets and on exit ramps facing the wrong direction.

teaching.text: Wrong-way ramps and one-way streets get this rule: do not go in. Remember: Wrong way, do not enter.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A Do Not Enter sign means you may not go in; it is posted on one-way streets and on exit ramps facing the wrong direction.

question.text: What does a Speed Limit sign give you?

answer.text: A Speed Limit sign gives the highest speed allowed when driving conditions are good.

teaching.text: The posted limit is the most you may drive in good conditions. Remember: Top speed in good conditions.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A Speed Limit sign gives the highest speed allowed when driving conditions are good.

question.text: What does a Reduced Speed Ahead sign tell you?

answer.text: A Reduced Speed Ahead sign tells you to slow down, for example because a slippery road may lie ahead.

teaching.text: Slow down because conditions ahead call for less speed. Remember: Slow down ahead.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A Reduced Speed Ahead sign tells you to slow down, for example because a slippery road may lie ahead.

question.text: What does a Reduced Speed Ahead regulatory sign tell you?

answer.text: Reduced Speed Ahead is a regulatory sign meaning you should slow down because a curb or slippery road might lie ahead.

teaching.text: Slippery When Wet warns; Reduced Speed Ahead is a rule. Remember: Slow down; curb or slick.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Reduced Speed Ahead is a regulatory sign meaning you should slow down because a curb or slippery road might lie ahead.

question.text: When does a school zone speed limit apply?

answer.text: On a school zone speed limit sign, the posted speed may not be exceeded whenever children can be seen.

teaching.text: When children are visible, the school speed limit is the maximum. Remember: Children visible, limit applies.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: On a school zone speed limit sign, the posted speed may not be exceeded whenever children can be seen.

question.text: What does a Keep Right sign mean?

answer.text: A Keep Right sign means a traffic island or other obstacle divides the road ahead.

teaching.text: An island or obstacle splits the road, so keep to its right. Remember: Island ahead, keep right.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A Keep Right sign means a traffic island or other obstacle divides the road ahead.

question.text: How does a No Turn sign differ from a No U-turn sign?

answer.text: A No Turn sign points toward the direction you may not turn, while a No U-turn sign forbids turning around.

teaching.text: One forbids a turn direction; the other forbids turning around. Remember: No turn that way; no turnaround.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A No Turn sign points toward the direction you may not turn, while a No U-turn sign forbids turning around.
audio_scripts.must_match_memory_hook: No turn that way; no turnaround

question.text: On a roundabout lane-use sign, what do the dot and the lines mean?

answer.text: On a roundabout lane-use sign, the dot on the left-turn arrow stands for the center of the roundabout and the lines show the separate lanes.

teaching.text: The dot marks the center of the roundabout, and the lines mark the lanes. Remember: Dot is center; lines are lanes.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: On a roundabout lane-use sign, the dot on the left-turn arrow stands for the center of the roundabout and the lines show the separate lanes.
audio_scripts.must_match_memory_hook: Dot is center; lines are lanes

question.text: In the two-lane roundabout example, what may each lane do?

answer.text: In the two-lane roundabout example, the left lane is only for turning left or making a U-turn, and the right lane is for going straight or turning right.

teaching.text: In that example the left lane turns left or U-turns, and the right lane goes straight or right. Remember: Left turns left; right goes straight.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: In the two-lane roundabout example, the left lane is only for turning left or making a U-turn, and the right lane is for going straight or turning right.
audio_scripts.must_match_memory_hook: Left turns left; right goes straight

question.text: In the three-lane roundabout example, what may each lane do?

answer.text: In the three-lane roundabout example, the far-left lane turns left or goes straight, the middle lane goes straight, and the right lane turns right.

teaching.text: In the three-lane example, each lane has its own job. Remember: Left, middle, right each differ.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: In the three-lane roundabout example, the far-left lane turns left or goes straight, the middle lane goes straight, and the right lane turns right.

question.text: In the second two-lane roundabout sign example, how are the two lanes used?

answer.text: In the second two-lane roundabout lane-use sign example, the far-left lane is used only to turn left while the right lane is used to turn left or go straight.

teaching.text: The layouts differ, so read the arrows every time. Remember: Left only; right left-or-straight.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: In the second two-lane roundabout lane-use sign example, the far-left lane is used only to turn left while the right lane is used to turn left or go straight.

question.text: What does a Stop sign look like, and what must you do?

answer.text: A Stop sign has eight sides and is red with white letters; come to a full stop and wait until your path is clear before going on.

teaching.text: Eight sides and red mean a full stop until your path is clear. Remember: Eight sides: full stop.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A Stop sign has eight sides and is red with white letters; come to a full stop and wait until your path is clear before going on.

question.text: What does a Yield sign look like, and what does it require?

answer.text: A Yield sign is a red and white triangle pointing down with red letters, and it means you must give the right-of-way to other vehicles.

teaching.text: A downward red and white triangle means give the right-of-way. Remember: Down triangle: give way.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A Yield sign is a red and white triangle pointing down with red letters, and it means you must give the right-of-way to other vehicles.

question.text: How do a Stop sign and a Yield sign differ in shape and meaning?

answer.text: A Stop sign is red with white letters and eight sides and requires a complete stop, while a Yield sign is a downward red and white triangle that requires giving the right-of-way to other vehicles.

teaching.text: Octagon means stop; downward triangle means yield. Remember: Octagon stops; triangle yields.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A Stop sign is red with white letters and eight sides and requires a complete stop, while a Yield sign is a downward red and white triangle that requires giving the right-of-way to other vehicles.

question.text: What does a Slow Moving Vehicle emblem look like, and what does it tell you?

answer.text: A Slow Moving Vehicle emblem is a triangle with reflective orange markings, and the vehicle carrying it may be moving at twenty-five miles per hour or less.

teaching.text: The orange triangle marks a vehicle that may be crawling along. Remember: Orange triangle, slow vehicle.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A Slow Moving Vehicle emblem is a triangle with reflective orange markings, and the vehicle carrying it may be moving at twenty-five miles per hour or less.

question.text: What does a No Passing Zone sign look like, and what does it mean?

answer.text: A No Passing Zone sign is a yellow pennant with black letters, and you may not pass any vehicle within that zone.

teaching.text: The yellow pennant marks a stretch where you may not pass. Remember: Yellow pennant, no passing.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A No Passing Zone sign is a yellow pennant with black letters, and you may not pass any vehicle within that zone.

question.text: How does the slow moving vehicle triangle differ from the no passing pennant?

answer.text: The orange Slow Moving Vehicle triangle marks a vehicle that may travel at twenty-five miles per hour or less, while the yellow No Passing Zone pennant forbids passing.

teaching.text: Orange triangle for slow vehicles, yellow pennant for no passing. Remember: Triangle slow; pennant no passing.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The orange Slow Moving Vehicle triangle marks a vehicle that may travel at twenty-five miles per hour or less, while the yellow No Passing Zone pennant forbids passing.

question.text: Who may use a reserved parking space?

answer.text: A reserved parking space may be used only by a vehicle with a valid disabled parking identification permit or a valid disabled license plate.

teaching.text: Reserved spaces need a valid disabled permit or plate. Remember: Disabled permit or plate only.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A reserved parking space may be used only by a vehicle with a valid disabled parking identification permit or a valid disabled license plate.

question.text: What do construction signs look like, and what do they warn about?

answer.text: Construction signs are orange diamonds or rectangles with black letters and symbols that warn of construction, maintenance or emergency workers on or near the road.

teaching.text: Orange diamonds or rectangles mean workers are on or near the road. Remember: Orange signs, workers near.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Construction signs are orange diamonds or rectangles with black letters and symbols that warn of construction, maintenance or emergency workers on or near the road.

question.text: What do orange diamond or rectangular construction signs warn drivers about?

answer.text: Orange diamond or rectangular construction signs have black lettering and symbols that warn about construction, maintenance, or emergency workers on or near the road.

teaching.text: Yellow is for road hazards; orange is for people working. Remember: Orange warns of road workers.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Orange diamond or rectangular construction signs have black lettering and symbols that warn about construction, maintenance, or emergency workers on or near the road.

question.text: What should you do when you see orange signs, cones and flags?

answer.text: Orange signs, cones and flags around a work area are your cue to slow down.

teaching.text: Cones, flags and orange signs are your cue to slow down. Remember: Orange means slow down.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Orange signs, cones and flags around a work area are your cue to slow down.

question.text: What happens to traffic fines in construction work areas?

answer.text: Traffic fines are doubled in construction work areas.

teaching.text: Every fine in a work zone counts double. Remember: Work zone fines double.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Traffic fines are doubled in construction work areas.

question.text: When may you use a cellphone in a construction zone?

answer.text: In a construction zone you may use a cellphone only to report an emergency.

teaching.text: In a work zone, the phone is for emergency reports only. Remember: Emergency calls only.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: In a construction zone you may use a cellphone only to report an emergency.

question.text: What does a Flagger Ahead sign warn of, and what must you do?

answer.text: A Road Construction Flagger Ahead sign warns of a worker with a sign or flag, and you must follow that worker's directions.

teaching.text: A flagger's signal must be followed. Remember: Follow the flagger.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A Road Construction Flagger Ahead sign warns of a worker with a sign or flag, and you must follow that worker's directions.

question.text: What do Road Workers Ahead and Road Work Ahead signs ask you to do?

answer.text: Road Workers Ahead and Road Work Ahead signs both call for you to slow down or move over, and the Road Work Ahead sign says how far away the work is.

teaching.text: Slow down or move over, and read how far ahead the work is. Remember: Slow down or move over.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Road Workers Ahead and Road Work Ahead signs both call for you to slow down or move over, and the Road Work Ahead sign says how far away the work is.

question.text: How does a flagger's direction differ from a Road Workers Ahead sign?

answer.text: A flagger's directions must be followed, while the Road Workers Ahead sign asks you to slow down or move over for workers ahead.

teaching.text: The flagger directs you; the sign only asks you to slow or move over. Remember: Flagger directs; sign warns.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A flagger's directions must be followed, while the Road Workers Ahead sign asks you to slow down or move over for workers ahead.

question.text: What do destination signs look like, and what do they show?

answer.text: Destination signs are square or rectangular, green or brown with white letters, and give directions and distances to places such as cities, states, airports, parks, historical sites and museums.

teaching.text: Green or brown signs with white letters point you toward places. Remember: Green or brown, places ahead.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Destination signs are square or rectangular, green or brown with white letters, and give directions and distances to places such as cities, states, airports, parks, historical sites and museums.

question.text: What does the arrow on an Exit sign show?

answer.text: On an Exit sign the arrow shows which side of the road the exit is on.

teaching.text: The exit arrow tells you which side to move toward. Remember: Arrow shows exit side.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: On an Exit sign the arrow shows which side of the road the exit is on.

question.text: What does a roundabout exit sign tell you?

answer.text: A roundabout exit sign tells you which road you will be on after leaving the roundabout at each exit.

teaching.text: Each exit sign names the road you will be on after you leave the roundabout. Remember: Which road each exit leads.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A roundabout exit sign tells you which road you will be on after leaving the roundabout at each exit.

question.text: Where are street name signs found, and how are they mounted?

answer.text: Street name signs stand on almost every corner, mounted on top of a silver pole that faces the road they name.

teaching.text: Look to the silver pole on the corner for the street's name. Remember: Silver pole, every corner.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Street name signs stand on almost every corner, mounted on top of a silver pole that faces the road they name.

question.text: What do brown destination signs point to?

answer.text: Brown destination signs point to recreational or scenic places, and some list the miles to get there.

teaching.text: Brown points to parks and other fun or scenic places. Remember: Brown means fun places.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Brown destination signs point to recreational or scenic places, and some list the miles to get there.

question.text: How do brown guide signs differ from green ones?

answer.text: Green and brown guide signs both give directions to places, but the brown ones point to fun or scenic places such as parks.

teaching.text: Brown is the scenic version of the green guide sign. Remember: Brown scenic, green general.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Green and brown guide signs both give directions to places, but the brown ones point to fun or scenic places such as parks.

question.text: What do service signs look like, and what do they point to?

answer.text: Service signs are square or rectangular, blue with white letters or symbols, and guide you to nearby services such as camping or a hospital.

teaching.text: Blue signs lead you to services such as hospitals and camping. Remember: Blue means services.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Service signs are square or rectangular, blue with white letters or symbols, and guide you to nearby services such as camping or a hospital.

question.text: How do blue signs differ from green and brown signs?

answer.text: Blue signs point to services such as a hospital or camping, while green and brown signs point to destinations.

teaching.text: Blue for services, green and brown for destinations. Remember: Blue services; green, brown places.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Blue signs point to services such as a hospital or camping, while green and brown signs point to destinations.

question.text: What are mile markers, and how do they help?

answer.text: Mile markers, also called reference markers, are tall, thin blue or green signs with white letters that show where you are on the road and help emergency crews reach highway incidents faster.

teaching.text: Mile markers pinpoint your location and speed up emergency help. Remember: Tall thin markers help responders.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Mile markers, also called reference markers, are tall, thin blue or green signs with white letters that show where you are on the road and help emergency crews reach highway incidents faster.

question.text: What does each mile marker show, and how often do they appear?

answer.text: Each mile marker gives the travel direction, route number and mile number, and markers are spaced every one to two-tenths of a mile on the right side of the road or in the median.

teaching.text: Direction, route and mile number appear on every marker. Remember: Direction, route, mile number.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Each mile marker gives the travel direction, route number and mile number, and markers are spaced every one to two-tenths of a mile on the right side of the road or in the median.

question.text: How do you recognize a mile marker if it can be blue or green?

answer.text: Mile markers can be blue or green but are recognized by their tall, thin shape and the direction, route and mile number they carry.

teaching.text: Tall, thin and numbered means a mile marker, whatever the color. Remember: Tall, thin, mile numbers.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Mile markers can be blue or green but are recognized by their tall, thin shape and the direction, route and mile number they carry.

question.text: Why do route number signs come in different shapes and colors?

answer.text: Route number signs change shape and color with the type of road and help you follow a route to your destination.

teaching.text: The marker's shape and color tell you the type of road. Remember: Shape tells road type.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Route number signs change shape and color with the type of road and help you follow a route to your destination.

question.text: What does an Interstate highway sign look like?

answer.text: An Interstate highway sign is a shield, red on top and blue on the bottom, with white lettering.

teaching.text: Red on top and blue below means an interstate. Remember: Red-top, blue-bottom shield.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: An Interstate highway sign is a shield, red on top and blue on the bottom, with white lettering.

question.text: What does a county road sign look like?

answer.text: A county road sign is a white rectangle with rounded edges and black letters.

teaching.text: A white rounded rectangle marks a county road. Remember: Rounded rectangle, county.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A county road sign is a white rectangle with rounded edges and black letters.

question.text: What does a U.S. route sign look like?

answer.text: A U.S. route sign looks like a police badge and is usually grey or white with black letters, unlike the red and blue interstate shield.

teaching.text: The badge shape marks a U.S. route, unlike the red and blue interstate shield. Remember: Police badge, U.S. route.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A U.S. route sign looks like a police badge and is usually grey or white with black letters, unlike the red and blue interstate shield.

question.text: What does a state road sign look like?

answer.text: A state road sign is shaped like a milk jug with its spout at the bottom and is white with black letters.

teaching.text: The milk jug shape marks a state road. Remember: Milk jug, state road.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A state road sign is shaped like a milk jug with its spout at the bottom and is white with black letters.

question.text: Which three railroad crossing mistakes must you never make?

answer.text: Never race a train to a crossing, never stop on the tracks, and do not start across unless there is room for your vehicle on the far side.

teaching.text: Never race, never stop on the rails, and never cross without room beyond. Remember: Never race, stop, or squeeze.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Never race a train to a crossing, never stop on the tracks, and do not start across unless there is room for your vehicle on the far side.

question.text: What should you avoid while crossing tracks, and when should you look both ways?

answer.text: Do not change gears while you are crossing railroad tracks, and look both ways before crossing even when the crossing lights are not flashing.

teaching.text: Stay in one gear across the tracks, and look both ways every time. Remember: Same gear; always look.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Do not change gears while you are crossing railroad tracks, and look both ways before crossing even when the crossing lights are not flashing.

question.text: How do trains compare with how fast they seem?

answer.text: Trains are big and heavy and travel faster than they appear to.

teaching.text: A train is closer and faster than it looks. Remember: Faster than they look.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Trains are big and heavy and travel faster than they appear to.

question.text: What does the round yellow railroad warning sign tell you?

answer.text: The railroad advance warning sign is round and yellow with an X symbol and black letters, telling you a crossing is ahead and to watch for a train.

teaching.text: The round yellow sign with an X means a crossing is ahead. Remember: Round yellow, crossing ahead.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The railroad advance warning sign is round and yellow with an X symbol and black letters, telling you a crossing is ahead and to watch for a train.

question.text: At a crossbuck with flashing lights, when may you go?

answer.text: At a crossbuck with flashing lights, the lights flash when a train approaches from either direction; wait until they stop and the track is clear before going.

teaching.text: Flashing lights mean a train is coming from either side; wait until they stop. Remember: Lights stop, track clear.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: At a crossbuck with flashing lights, the lights flash when a train approaches from either direction; wait until they stop and the track is clear before going.

question.text: What does a crossbuck with a Yield sign below it mean?

answer.text: A white X-shaped crossbuck with a Yield sign mounted below it means you must yield to any train using the crossing.

teaching.text: A Yield sign under the crossbuck means trains go first. Remember: Yield to any train.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A white X-shaped crossbuck with a Yield sign mounted below it means you must yield to any train using the crossing.

question.text: How does the round railroad warning sign differ from the crossbuck?

answer.text: The round yellow railroad warning sign with an X tells you a crossing is there, while the white X-shaped crossbuck also lists how many tracks you will cross.

teaching.text: The round sign warns ahead; the crossbuck at the tracks counts them. Remember: Round warns; crossbuck counts tracks.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The round yellow railroad warning sign with an X tells you a crossing is there, while the white X-shaped crossbuck also lists how many tracks you will cross.

question.text: What do the Tracks out-of-service and Exempt plaques mean?

answer.text: A Tracks out-of-service sign means the tracks are no longer used, while an Exempt sign means only certain vehicles are excused from stopping before crossing.

teaching.text: Out-of-service means unused tracks; Exempt excuses only some vehicles. Remember: Unused tracks; some vehicles excused.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A Tracks out-of-service sign means the tracks are no longer used, while an Exempt sign means only certain vehicles are excused from stopping before crossing.

question.text: What is the blue Report Problem or Emergency sign for?

answer.text: A blue Report Problem or Emergency sign with white letters stands at every highway-railroad crossing and lists a phone number for reporting a stalled vehicle on the tracks or a failed warning light.

teaching.text: The blue sign's phone number is for reporting a stuck vehicle or a broken warning light. Remember: Call about crossing problems.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A blue Report Problem or Emergency sign with white letters stands at every highway-railroad crossing and lists a phone number for reporting a stalled vehicle on the tracks or a failed warning light.

question.text: Does every multi-track crossing post a number-of-tracks sign?

answer.text: Some crossings with more than one track post a number-of-tracks sign, but not all do, so always check for additional tracks before you cross.

teaching.text: Missing track-count signs do not prove there is only one track. Remember: Always check for more tracks.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Some crossings with more than one track post a number-of-tracks sign, but not all do, so always check for additional tracks before you cross.

question.text: When a train passes at a crossing with two sets of tracks, when may you go?

answer.text: When a crossing has two sets of tracks, wait until the train is far enough away that you can see the other tracks are clear.

teaching.text: After a train passes, wait until you can see every track is clear. Remember: Wait until you see clear.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: When a crossing has two sets of tracks, wait until the train is far enough away that you can see the other tracks are clear.

question.text: What must you never do at a railroad gate?

answer.text: A railroad gate comes down when a train approaches; never drive around it or under it while it is moving up or down.

teaching.text: A moving gate means stay put; never go around or under it. Remember: Never go around a gate.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A railroad gate comes down when a train approaches; never drive around it or under it while it is moving up or down.

question.text: When may you cross at a crossing with a bell or horn?

answer.text: Where a crossing has a bell or horn with its lights, do not cross until the sound has stopped.

teaching.text: Wait for the bell or horn to fall silent before crossing. Remember: Wait for silence.
